TextBlock.Text: THEATRE The Biak enclave
DATE 14 November 2028 · 0410 local
SIDE Royal Australian Navy
WINDOW 90 min, closes at 135
E-7A Wedgetail — RAAF. Photo: U.S. Air Force photo by Lawrence Crespo · Public domain · cropped
"Air superiority is not guaranteed. It must be earned every day."
- Gen. Kenneth S. Wilsbach, Chief of Staff, US Air Force, 2025

THE BIAK ENCLAVE, 0410. Since The Open Door the enclave has had three nights of Russian transports. Imagery shows an S-350 Vityaz battery with its 50N6 radar west of the field, an S-300PMU2 launcher with its 30N6E2 to the east, a Buk-M3 on the northern ridge and a Nebo-U early-warning radar on the coast above them all. An Iskander-M launcher arrived last night.

The package is two hundred miles south over New Guinea: DOOM 41 and 42, B-52H out of Tindal with ARRW; GRIZZLY 31 and 32, RAAF Growlers with AGM-88G; EAGLE II 21 and 22 as escort; and WEDGETAIL 04 for the picture. The S-300 reaches a hundred miles and the S-350 sixty-five; stay outside both until the Growlers have a fix.

The win is the two engagement radars. Two J-16s are on the enclave field and will be up within ten minutes of the first emission. A relief ship is in the anchorage south of the field: she is not a target, and neither is the town.
Wing Commander Daniel Ward, Air Component, RAAF Tindal; Colonel Dale Rourke, USAF, for the bombers
COMMANDER'S INTENT

The Open Door got the relief through and cost them a battery. They have replaced it with better: an S-350 and an S-300PMU2 under a Nebo-U, and a Buk-M3 for the low end. Everything the enclave launches south from here on flies under that umbrella. Take the two engagement radars and the launchers are blind; take the Iskander while you are there and nobody will complain. The bombers are borrowed from Guam and I want them back.
• Destroy the S-350's 50N6 radar and the S-300's 30N6E2
• Destroy the Buk-M3
• Destroy the Nebo-U radar
• Destroy the Iskander-M launcher
• Lose neither B-52
• Harm no relief shipping

Two B-52H with ARRW, two RAAF EA-18G, two F-15EX, an E-7A Wedgetail. Opposing: an S-350 battery (50N6 radar and a launcher), an S-300PMU2 (30N6E2 and a launcher), a Buk-M3, a Nebo-U radar, an Iskander-M launcher and two J-16. Neutral: a relief ship in the anchorage.

The planned window is 90 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 45 minutes more; the operation is closed at 135 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
